claims.statement: Verified fact: AFIR distinguishes charge-point operators from mobility service providers and requires transparent, session-specific price information for public charging.
Verified fact: AFIR and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/655 require harmonized access to specified public charging-infrastructure data through APIs and national access points.

Verified fact: the Commission's AFIR guidance says mandatory e-roaming participation was considered and discarded to preserve operators' contractual freedom; private CDR and agreement access therefore cannot be assumed from AFIR.

Verified fact: OCPI 2.3 CDRs already support relevant tariffs, charging periods, total cost, energy, optional signed data, and an invoice reference; OICP 2.3 likewise carries session, tariff identifier, energy, and optional signed-meter evidence.

Verified fact: Gireve already offers CDR quality checks, agreement-based price calculation, B2B invoice generation, payment tracking, and dispute management, closely overlapping the proposed workflow.

Verified fact: Hubject Financial Services supports OCPI/OICP CDR invoicing across the EU27 and neighboring EEA markets, charges CPOs a percentage transaction fee, requires an active agreement and onboarding, and issues invoices in the CPO's name.

Evidence-supported inference: a defensible entry wedge must reconcile direct or multi-platform feeds and preserve evidence that a customer's existing hub does not already provide; basic CDR normalization and invoice generation are not differentiated.
Unknown: smaller EU operators' uncovered dispute rates, willingness to authorize private feeds, and willingness to pay a neutral entrant have not been verified.

contrary_evidence: Gireve's current clearing offer already performs CDR quality checks, agreement-based price calculation, B2B invoicing, dispute management, and payment tracking, leaving little novelty in the proposed core: https://www.gireve.com/clearing-services/

Hubject Financial Services accepts OCPI CDRs, covers the EU27 plus nearby markets, charges a transaction percentage, and produces CPO-issued B2B invoices: https://support.hubject.com/hc/en-us/articles/26990001350813-FAQ-CPO

OCPI 2.3 and OICP 2.3 encode many elements of the proposed canonical record, including tariffs, costs, energy, session identity, and optional signed-meter data: https://github.com/ocpi/ocpi/blob/2.3.0/release/core/mod_cdrs.asciidoc

The Commission states that mandatory e-roaming was discarded, so AFIR creates no compulsory private-feed channel for an entrant: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/clean-transport/alternative-fuels-sustainable-mobility-europe/alternative-fuels-infrastructure/questions-and-answers-regulation-deployment-alternative-fuels-infrastructure-eu-20231804_en

Hubject still supports manual reconciliation for off-platform or partial payments, which shows residual exceptions but also shows that incumbents can add the same exception tooling: https://support.hubject.com/hc/en-us/articles/30230734894877-Invoice-Manual-Reconciliation

economics.acquisition_route: Run one contract-authorized, read-only reconciliation pilot for a Polish CPO/eMSP pair that uses a direct or multi-platform relationship, ideally through one back-office integrator. Channel willingness and access have not been validated.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unknown. No evidence-backed founder-wealth timing can be stated before pricing, retention, integration cost, and obtainable customer count are validated. Recompute any path only from contracted recurring revenue and measured contribution margin without double-counting retained earnings.
economics.founder_time: Planning constraint: at most 4-5 hours/day for one integration. This is not yet shown sufficient; bespoke feed mapping or dispute operations may require contracted protocol and tax expertise.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown. No reviewed source supports the prior 72-86% estimate. A pilot model must include protocol mapping, VAT configuration support boundaries, security, dispute review, and manual reconciliation before claiming software margins.
economics.payback: Unknown. Measure historical manual handling cost, disputed value, prevented write-offs, and time-to-resolution against all onboarding and support cost; no reviewed evidence establishes a 6-9 month payback.
economics.pricing: Unknown. Hubject discloses a transaction fee equal to a small percentage of payout volume, while Gireve advertises zero connection fees for an already-connected CPO; neither source validates the earlier PLN monthly or per-session range. Do not quote a price until a buyer test measures uncovered exception value.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Charging sessions and periodic invoices recur, but retention is only an inference. An incumbent hub can absorb the same workflow, so renewal must depend on demonstrably cross-platform evidence or exception coverage.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a permissioned library of protocol, tariff, and agreement edge cases can improve straight-through reconciliation, while bilateral mappings and dispute history can raise switching costs
fingerprint.customer: small and mid-sized EU charge-point operators, e-mobility service providers, and cross-border fleet charging programs whose private session data spans direct bilateral links, more than one hub, or an uncovered back-office workflow
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: charger back-office integrators, hardware distributors, fleet-management vendors, and one-corridor technical pilots; no channel commitment is yet evidenced
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: independent OCPI/OICP-adjacent normalization, tariff-and-agreement version archive, accounting-only bilateral netting, and dispute-evidence API; usage software without funds custody
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: CPO, mobility provider, or fleet manager pays for an accepted cleared-session record or closed roaming statement after a pilot demonstrates that the gateway resolves exceptions not already handled by its incumbent platform
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a roaming statement, fleet invoice, or end-user dispute where tariff components, session identity, delivered kWh, or payment status do not align

founder_fit: Data normalization, anomaly detection, and evidence lineage fit the founder's technical profile.
An API-first B2B product avoids camera exposure and consumer-influencer distribution.
A single read-only pilot can fit available capital if access is granted before substantial build spend.
The founder can begin in Poland and use EU protocol knowledge, but has no evidenced CPO/eMSP channel or roaming rights.
A bespoke first integration may exceed part-time capacity, so protocol, VAT, and security work must be bounded or contracted.
risks: Gireve and Hubject already bundle CDR validation, tariff calculation, invoicing, dispute handling, reconciliation, and payment tracking.
OCPI 2.3 and OICP 2.3 already encode much of the proposed canonical record, including tariff, session, cost, meter, and optional signed-meter fields.
AFIR does not compel participation in e-roaming, and its public-data rules do not grant access to private CDRs or bilateral agreements.
Private session and identity data are contract- and data-protection-sensitive; the product cannot operate from public AFIR feeds alone.
Cross-border VAT configuration and invoice correctness remain the CPO's responsibility and can create liability if product boundaries are unclear.
A low-priced incumbent transaction fee or zero connection fee for existing hub users can compress entrant willingness to pay.
Protocol fragmentation and dispute review can turn the product into integration and managed services rather than scalable software.
Long enterprise integration and trust cycles may conflict with part-time founder availability.

structure.control_point: evidence-grade canonical charge-detail record binding identity, tariff and agreement version, meter values, and invoice line
structure.critical_dependency: contractual access to private CPO and mobility-provider session feeds with trustworthy meter values and stable roaming identifiers

thesis: Offer small charge-point operators, mobility-service providers, and commercial fleets a neutral, non-custodial gateway that ingests contractually authorized OCPI, OICP, or bespoke charge-detail-record feeds; preserves the applicable tariff and agreement version; reconciles session identity and signed-meter evidence; and produces invoice-ready bilateral statements and dispute packets. Research narrows the initial use case to direct or multi-platform roaming relationships where an existing hub does not already provide the complete workflow. The product would not hold funds, provide tax advice, or decide disputes.
title: Evidence-Grade EV Roaming Charge Clearing Gateway
uncertainties: No independent evidence quantifies disputed-session frequency, value, or handling cost for the target small and mid-sized EU segment.
No target operator has confirmed that an incumbent hub leaves a sufficiently valuable cross-platform reconciliation gap.
The number of obtainable Polish or CEE private-feed relationships is unknown.
It is unknown whether counterparties will accept an entrant's canonical record as dispute evidence.
Customer budget ownership, sales cycle, onboarding effort, security requirements, and churn are unknown.
The lawful boundary among accounting netting, invoice generation, tax configuration, and regulated payment activity requires counsel before scope expansion.
The PLN 75,000 capital figure is a planning cap, not an evidence-based build cost.
